About Me

About Me

I’m MD Shahid Hussain, an IT professional, corporate trainer, and entrepreneur with 15 years of experience across technology services, enterprise systems, and professional learning. I hold a Master of Computer Applications (MCA) from Pune University.

My career has been shaped by a simple belief: technology creates value when people can rely on it, understand it, and use it to improve their work. That belief has guided me through technical support, Oracle database and applications administration, corporate training, resource coordination, and business leadership.

A Career Across Technology and Learning

My technical background includes Oracle Apps DBA, Oracle database administration, and IT support. These roles have taught me to investigate problems carefully, support important business systems, and explain technical matters in ways that help people make informed decisions.

Corporate training has also been a significant part of my journey. I have worked to connect organisations with technology trainers and learning resources, support training engagements, and make complex subjects easier for professionals to understand and apply. This combination of IT and training experience helps me see both how a system works and what people need to use it confidently.

Leadership and Entrepreneurship

I previously served as Director and CEO of ANT GLOBAL SOFT PRIVATE LIMITED and AMOLI JEWELLERS PRIVATE LIMITED. These roles gave me firsthand experience in building businesses, coordinating teams, managing relationships, and making decisions under real operating constraints.

At ANT GLOBAL SOFT, my work was connected to corporate IT training and technology services. My leadership role at AMOLI JEWELLERS broadened my understanding of business operations and customer needs.

These are former roles. I am no longer involved in either company, and both companies have put their services on hold. The experience of leading them continues to shape how I approach challenges and opportunities.

My Focus Today

I am expanding my expertise in AI Product Management, product and design thinking, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AI Agents, Agentic AI, prompt engineering, and AI automation. I am especially interested in practical AI use cases that help organisations improve workflows, find information, and support better decisions.

I hope to bring my background in enterprise technology, training, and business operations into product work. My approach begins with understanding the people affected by a problem, then shaping a solution that is useful, responsible, and grounded in real needs.

A Purpose Beyond Business

During the COVID-19 period, I helped organise ration distribution in villages, reaching more than 500 people. That experience reinforced something I believe deeply: meaningful work should improve lives, especially for people who have limited access to support.

My long-term aim is to build a school and a hospital that serve families with limited financial means. I want children to have access to quality education and families to receive dependable medical care, either free of cost or at a price they can afford. This vision includes people living in poverty as well as middle-class families who may struggle with the rising cost of education and healthcare.

I know this is an ambitious goal that will take time, resources, and the right partners. It is a goal I want to work toward throughout my life, because a person’s financial circumstances should not determine the quality of education or medical care they can receive.

What Drives Me

My professional experience brings together technical operations, corporate learning, entrepreneurship, and emerging AI products. My personal ambition gives that work a wider purpose. I want to keep learning, build useful solutions, and create opportunities that make a lasting difference for people and communities.

Digital Marketing & Media Services

Digital marketing works best when every activity serves a clear purpose. A business needs to know whom it wants to reach, what it wants to communicate, and what action it hopes people will take. My interest in digital marketing is rooted in that connection between business goals, useful content, and measurable results.

Drawing on my experience in IT, corporate training, and business coordination, I am particularly interested in digital marketing for technology companies, training providers, educational institutions, and professional services organisations. The following are planned service areas.

1. Digital Marketing Strategy

A practical marketing plan begins with an understanding of the organisation, its audience, and its goals. This area would cover audience research, positioning, channel selection, campaign objectives, content themes, and a publishing plan. The aim would be to give each activity a defined role, whether it supports awareness, enquiries, event registrations, or stronger relationships with existing audiences.

2. Social Media Management

A professional social presence should communicate consistently and give people a reason to follow or engage. This area would include profile reviews, content calendars, post coordination, community engagement, and performance reviews for relevant platforms such as LinkedIn, Facebook, and Instagram. The choice of platform and content would depend on the organisation’s audience and objectives.

3. Content Creation and Brand Communication

Clear content helps an organisation explain what it does and why it matters. Planned content formats include social posts, service descriptions, educational articles, campaign messages, event announcements, brochures, and short video scripts. My focus would be on making technical or specialised offerings understandable while preserving their professional credibility.

4. Brand Identity and Digital Presence

People should be able to recognise an organisation and understand its message wherever they encounter it. This area would cover the coordination of page descriptions, visual direction, tone of voice, key messages, and campaign materials. The goal would be a consistent presentation across social profiles, websites, and promotional content.

5. Search Visibility and Website Content

A website should be easy to find, easy to understand, and easy to use. This planned area would include reviewing page titles and descriptions, organising service pages, improving the clarity of website copy, and identifying technical or content issues that affect search visibility. Search performance and indexing information would help guide priorities.

6. Paid Social Campaigns

Paid campaigns can help an organisation reach a defined audience when there is a clear offer and a way to assess results. This area would involve campaign planning, audience and message development, creative coordination, landing page alignment, and performance review. Potential uses include promoting training programmes, events, services, and enquiry forms.

7. Lead Generation and Follow-Up

An enquiry is useful only when it reaches the right team and receives an appropriate response. This planned service would connect campaign messages with enquiry forms, landing pages, lead tracking, and follow-up workflows. For training providers, this could support demo registrations, course enquiries, corporate training requests, or partnership discussions.

8. Email Campaigns and Audience Nurturing

Email can help an organisation continue a useful conversation with people who have chosen to hear from it. This area would include audience grouping, newsletter planning, event invitations, follow-up messages, and campaign reporting. The emphasis would be on sending relevant information to the right audience at the right stage of their relationship with the organisation.

9. Reporting and Improvement

Digital activity should be reviewed against its original goal. Reporting would bring together relevant measures such as reach, engagement, website visits, enquiries, registrations, and campaign costs. The purpose would be to understand what is working, identify where people lose interest, and make informed improvements over time.

By MD Shahid Hussain · Career & Learning

From Oracle Apps DBA to AI Product Management: Building on Experience, Learning for the Future

Throughout my career, I have worked across IT support, Oracle database and application administration, corporate training, trainer coordination, and business leadership. Each role has helped me understand a different part of how organizations operate—from maintaining technology systems to coordinating people, addressing client requirements, and managing business responsibilities.

Today, I am bringing these perspectives together as I develop my capabilities in AI Product Management.

This transition involves a substantial learning commitment. My previous experience provides a useful foundation, while AI introduces new questions about data quality, model behaviour, evaluation, privacy, and human oversight. Understanding these questions is an essential part of learning to build products that people can depend on.

My Professional Foundation: Technology, People, and Operations

With an MCA from Pune University and more than 15 years of experience across technology, training, and business roles, I have had opportunities to observe how technical decisions affect everyday operations.

In IT support, I learned the importance of listening carefully, identifying the immediate problem, and communicating in language users could understand. A technical explanation becomes useful when it helps someone continue their work or make an informed decision.

My Oracle Apps DBA experience strengthened my understanding of enterprise systems, troubleshooting, database operations, and the responsibility that comes with supporting business applications.

Corporate training and trainer coordination introduced another dimension: understanding learning requirements, identifying suitable expertise, aligning expectations, and coordinating delivery.

My previous roles as Director and CEO of ANT Global Soft Private Limited and Amoli Jewellers Private Limited broadened my exposure to administration, procurement, operations, client relationships, and resource decisions. I previously served in these positions and am no longer involved in the companies’ operations.

Together, these experiences have shaped the way I approach problems. I look at the technology involved, the people affected, and the operational conditions that determine whether a solution will work.

What Oracle Apps DBA Experience Contributes to Product Thinking

Enterprise applications support activities that matter to an organization: financial reporting, procurement, business transactions, and daily operations. When a system slows down or a process fails, the impact extends beyond the technical team.

A delayed financial report, for example, may affect a finance team’s schedule, create additional follow-up work, and postpone decisions. Understanding that impact changes the questions we ask.

Alongside investigating technical behaviour, we need to understand:

• Which users are affected?

• What business activity is being delayed?

• Does the problem occur regularly or under specific conditions?

• What evidence supports the suspected cause?

• What would users consider an acceptable outcome?

These questions connect operational support with product discovery.

One experience that informs my thinking involved an Oracle EBS General Ledger report that had previously completed in approximately 15 minutes but later took around 40 minutes, particularly during month-end activity.

The investigation included checks of alert logs, blocking sessions, indexes, code changes, and infrastructure conditions. Indexing and blocking were suspected contributors, but the actual cause was not conclusively established.

That distinction matters. A suspected explanation should remain a hypothesis until sufficient evidence supports it.

From a product perspective, this experience raises further questions about monitoring, visibility, escalation, and the information users receive during a delay. It illustrates how an operational issue can reveal opportunities to improve the wider user experience.

What Corporate Training Taught Me About User Needs

Corporate training requires more than selecting a topic and scheduling a trainer.

Organizations may need employees to perform a particular task, adopt a technology, or address a capability gap. Learners may have different levels of experience, confidence, and access to practice environments.

A suitable training engagement therefore begins with understanding the requirement:

What should participants be able to do afterwards? What do they already know? Which examples are relevant to their work? What support will they need to apply the learning?

Trainer coordination also requires clear communication between clients, trainers, learners, and internal teams. Unclear expectations can affect content, schedules, delivery quality, and the overall experience.

These lessons are relevant to product management. A feature can appear useful during planning and still fail to meet users’ needs. Early conversations, practical observation, and feedback help uncover the gap between what we assume people need and what they actually require.

How Business Leadership Shapes My Approach

Business leadership gave me exposure to decisions where multiple needs competed for limited resources.

Operations, procurement, administration, and client commitments are closely connected. A delay in one area can affect another. Decisions must account for cost, timing, capability, and the organization’s ability to deliver consistently.

This experience encourages me to consider the practical conditions around a proposed product.

Who will maintain it? What will implementation require? How will employees adopt it? Can the organization support the ongoing cost? What happens when something goes wrong?

In AI Product Management, these questions help establish whether an idea is operationally realistic. A promising demonstration is an early step; delivering dependable value requires continued attention to implementation, evaluation, and support.

Why I Am Focusing on AI Product Management

My interest in AI Product Management comes from a desire to connect technical possibilities with clearly defined business problems.

I am particularly interested in situations where people spend considerable time searching for information, handling repetitive enquiries, or working across disconnected systems.

AI may offer useful assistance in some of these situations. However, the first task is to understand the problem and assess whether AI is an appropriate approach.

For example, if customers receive inconsistent answers because an organization’s policies are outdated or contradictory, introducing an AI assistant will not resolve the underlying information problem. The source material needs attention first.

This is the kind of judgment I want to develop: identifying where AI can contribute, what conditions it requires, and how its usefulness should be assessed.

My Current Learning Priorities

I am developing my knowledge through a combination of technical learning and product thinking.

Learning areaWhat I am working to understand
Product discoveryIdentifying users, investigating problems, and testing assumptions
Design thinkingExploring needs and evaluating ideas through feedback
Python and APIsUnderstanding how applications process data and connect with services
Generative AI and LLMsUnderstanding capabilities, limitations, and possible applications
RAGExploring how applications retrieve relevant information to support generated responses
Prompt engineeringPractising clear instructions and examining the quality of outputs
PrototypingMaking ideas concrete enough to discuss, test, and improve
EvaluationDefining what a useful, accurate, and acceptable result looks like

These areas represent my current learning focus. I distinguish them from technologies and responsibilities in which I have established professional experience.

That transparency is important to me. A credible transition should demonstrate progress while remaining clear about the depth of capability developed so far.

Applying Product Thinking to Customer Support

Customer support is one area I am exploring because the problems are familiar and easy to recognize.

A customer explains an issue through WhatsApp, calls later for an update, and then receives an email asking for the same details. Different employees handle the conversation, but no one has complete context or clear responsibility for the next action.

Before proposing a solution, I would investigate how information moves through the organization.

Where are conversations recorded? How are issues assigned? What causes customers to repeat themselves? Which questions could be answered from approved documents? Which situations require human judgment?

Possible improvements might include clearer ownership, shared customer history, better knowledge management, and assistance with finding relevant guidance. AI could support selected parts of that workflow if the information and processes are ready.

I would also want to evaluate the outcome through measures such as response accuracy, resolution time, repeated customer contacts, escalation quality, and agent effort.

At present, this is an area of exploration and product thinking, rather than a claim of a completed deployment.

The Professional Approach I Want to Build

As I continue this journey, I want my work to reflect a few consistent principles:

• Understand the problem before committing to a solution.

• Support conclusions with evidence.

• Describe capabilities and limitations accurately.

• Consider data quality and operational readiness.

• Define when human review is necessary.

• Evaluate outcomes and learn from feedback.

These principles connect my earlier experience with the responsibilities I am learning to take on in AI Product Management.

My goal is to contribute to products that solve identifiable problems, fit organizational workflows, and earn users’ confidence through dependable behaviour.

Looking Ahead

I see this transition as an opportunity to build on my experience while remaining open to new methods, tools, and perspectives.

Oracle Apps DBA work taught me to investigate technical problems carefully. Corporate training taught me to understand requirements and coordinate delivery. Business leadership taught me to consider resources, commitments, and operational consequences.

AI Product Management gives me a direction in which to develop these lessons further.

I welcome conversations with professionals in enterprise technology, corporate learning, AI, and product management. Practical discussions, constructive feedback, and opportunities to collaborate can help turn learning into more informed work.

For enquiries about Oracle DBA support, corporate IT training, trainer coordination, or technology collaboration, please visit my portfolio and contact me to discuss your requirements.

In experiences ki wajah se main problem ko technology, affected logon aur practical operational conditions—teeno angles se dekhta hoon.

Oracle Apps DBA Experience se Product Thinking ko Kya Milta Hai

Enterprise applications financial reporting, procurement, business transactions aur daily operations ko support karti hain. System slow ho ya process fail ho, asar technical team se aage bhi jata hai.

Financial report late hone se finance team ka schedule disturb ho sakta hai, follow-up badh sakta hai aur decisions delay ho sakte hain. Is impact ko samajhne se hamare investigation ke sawaal bhi badalte hain.

Technical behaviour ke saath humein poochhna chahiye: kaunse users affect ho rahe hain? Kaunsa business activity delay ho raha hai? Problem regular hai ya specific conditions mein hoti hai? Suspected cause ke liye kya evidence hai? Users ke liye acceptable outcome kya hoga?

Ye sawaal operational support ko product discovery se jodte hain.

Ek experience mein Oracle EBS General Ledger report, jo pehle lagbhag 15 minutes mein complete hoti thi, baad mein kareeb 40 minutes lene lagi—khaaskar month-end activity ke dauraan.

Investigation mein alert logs, blocking sessions, indexes, code changes aur infrastructure conditions check kiye gaye. Indexing aur blocking possible contributors lage, lekin actual cause conclusively establish nahi hua.

Yeh farq zaroori hai: suspected explanation ko hypothesis hi kehna chahiye, jab tak sufficient evidence usse support na kare.

Product perspective se yeh experience monitoring, visibility, escalation aur delay ke dauraan users ko milne wali information par sawaal uthata hai. Operational issue wider user experience improve karne ke opportunities bhi dikha sakta hai.

Corporate Training se User Needs ke Baare Mein Kya Seekha

Corporate training sirf topic select karne aur trainer schedule karne tak limited nahi hai.

Organisation chahti ho sakti hai ki employees koi task kar saken, technology adopt karen ya capability gap ko address karen. Learners ka experience, confidence aur practice environments tak access alag ho sakta hai.

Achhi training requirement samajhne se shuru hoti hai: participants training ke baad kya kar saken? Woh pehle se kya jaante hain? Unke kaam ke liye kaunse examples relevant hain? Learning apply karne ke liye kya support chahiye?

Trainer coordination mein clients, trainers, learners aur internal teams ke beech clear communication zaroori hai. Unclear expectations content, schedules, delivery quality aur overall experience ko affect kar sakti hain.

Product management mein bhi ye lessons kaam aate hain. Planning mein useful lagne wala feature actual user needs ko miss kar sakta hai. Early conversations, practical observation aur feedback assumptions aur real requirements ke beech ka gap samajhne mein madad karte hain.

Business Leadership Mere Approach ko Kaise Shape Karti Hai

Business leadership mein aise decisions ka exposure mila jahan limited resources ke liye kai needs compete karti thi.

Operations, procurement, administration aur client commitments ek doosre se connected hain. Ek area ka delay doosre ko affect kar sakta hai. Decisions mein cost, timing, capability aur consistently deliver karne ki capacity dekhni padti hai.

Isliye proposed product ke saath main practical sawaal bhi dekhta hoon: ise maintain kaun karega? Implementation mein kya lagega? Employees ise kaise adopt karenge? Ongoing cost support ho payegi? Kuch galat hone par kya hoga?

AI Product Management mein ye sawaal idea ki operational practicality samajhne mein madad karte hain. Promising demonstration ek early step hai; dependable value ke liye implementation, evaluation aur support par lagataar dhyan chahiye.

Main AI Product Management par Focus Kyun Kar Raha Hoon

Meri interest technical possibilities ko clearly defined business problems se jodne mein hai.

Mujhe un situations mein khaas dilchaspi hai jahan log information dhoondhne, repetitive enquiries handle karne ya disconnected systems ke beech kaam karne mein bahut waqt lagate hain.

AI kuch situations mein useful assistance de sakta hai. Lekin pehla kaam problem samajhna aur assess karna hai ki AI suitable approach hai ya nahi.

Misal ke taur par, agar organisation ki policies outdated ya contradictory hain aur customers ko inconsistent answers milte hain, to AI assistant introduce karne se underlying information problem solve nahi hogi. Pehle source material ko theek karna hoga.

Main yahi judgment develop karna chahta hoon: AI kahan contribute kar sakta hai, uske liye kya conditions chahiye aur usefulness ko kaise assess kiya jaye.

Meri Current Learning Priorities

Main technical learning aur product thinking dono ke through apni knowledge develop kar raha hoon.

Product discovery: users pehchanna, problems investigate karna aur assumptions test karna.

Design thinking: needs explore karna aur feedback se ideas evaluate karna.

Python aur APIs: applications data kaise process karti hain aur services se kaise connect hoti hain, yeh samajhna.

Generative AI aur LLMs: capabilities, limitations aur possible applications samajhna.

RAG: generated responses ko support karne ke liye relevant information retrieve karne ka approach explore karna.

Prompt engineering: clear instructions practise karna aur outputs ki quality dekhna.

Prototyping: ideas ko itna concrete banana ki un par discussion, testing aur improvement ho sake.

Evaluation: useful, accurate aur acceptable result kaisa hoga, yeh define karna.

Ye meri current learning areas hain. Main inhe un technologies aur responsibilities se alag rakhta hoon jinmein mera established professional experience hai.

Yeh transparency mere liye important hai. Credible transition mein progress dikhni chahiye aur ab tak develop hui capability ki depth bhi clear honi chahiye.

Customer Support mein Product Thinking Apply Karna

Customer support ek area hai jise main explore kar raha hoon, kyunki iski problems familiar hain.

Customer WhatsApp par issue batata hai, update ke liye call karta hai, phir email mein usse wahi details dobara maangi jaati hain. Alag employees conversation handle karte hain, lekin complete context ya next action ki clear ownership kisi ke paas nahi hoti.

Solution propose karne se pehle main organisation mein information ka flow investigate karunga: conversations kahan record hoti hain? Issues assign kaise hote hain? Customer ko repeat kyun karna padta hai? Approved documents se kaunse answers mil sakte hain? Kin situations mein human judgment chahiye?

Possible improvements mein clearer ownership, shared customer history, better knowledge management aur relevant guidance dhoondhne mein assistance shamil ho sakti hai. Information aur processes ready hon to AI workflow ke selected parts ko support kar sakta hai.

Outcome evaluate karne ke liye response accuracy, resolution time, repeated customer contacts, escalation quality aur agent effort jaise measures dekhna chaahunga.

Filhaal yeh exploration aur product thinking ka area hai; ise completed deployment ka claim nahi samajhna chahiye.

Main Kaisa Professional Approach Banana Chahta Hoon

Solution choose karne se pehle problem samajhna. Conclusions ko evidence se support karna. Capabilities aur limitations accurately batana. Data quality aur operational readiness dekhna. Human review kab zaroori hai, yeh define karna. Outcomes evaluate karke feedback se seekhna.

Ye principles mere pehle ke experience ko AI Product Management ki un responsibilities se jodte hain jinhe main ab seekh raha hoon.

Mera goal aise products mein contribute karna hai jo identifiable problems solve karen, organisational workflows mein fit hon aur dependable behaviour se users ka confidence earn karen.

Aage ka Raasta

Main is transition ko apne experience par aage badhne aur naye methods, tools aur perspectives seekhne ka mauka maanta hoon.

Oracle Apps DBA work ne technical problems carefully investigate karna sikhaya. Corporate training ne requirements samajhna aur delivery coordinate karna sikhaya. Business leadership ne resources, commitments aur operational consequences dekhna sikhaya.

AI Product Management mujhe in lessons ko aur develop karne ki direction deta hai.

Enterprise technology, corporate learning, AI aur product management ke professionals se conversations ka swagat hai. Practical discussions, constructive feedback aur collaboration opportunities learning ko aur informed work mein badalne mein madad kar sakti hain.

Oracle DBA support, corporate IT training, trainer coordination ya technology collaboration ke enquiries ke liye mere portfolio ke Contact section se apni requirements discuss kar sakte hain.
